# Spherical Sparse Autoencoders

Exploring a **spherical** variant of sparse autoencoders (SAEs) for dense text
embeddings, following the setup of O'Neill et al., 2024 — *"Disentangling Dense
Embeddings with Sparse Autoencoders"* ([arXiv:2408.00657](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.00657),
PDF in `papers/`).

![Spherical SAE — the latent code is normalised before decoding, keeping only
the distribution of concepts and discarding magnitude.](assets/spherical_sae.png)

*Figure generated by `scripts/make_figure.py`.*

## The idea

A standard top-k SAE reconstructs an embedding with a linear decoder:

```
h  = TopK(W_e x + b_e)      # sparse latent code
x̂ = W_d h + b_d            # reconstruction
```

OpenAI / sentence-transformer embeddings are (or can be) **L2-normalised**, so
they live on the unit sphere `S^{d-1}`, and downstream semantic search uses
**cosine similarity** — only direction matters, not magnitude.

The spherical variant **normalises the latent code before the decoder**:

```
h̃ = normalize(h)           # L2 -> sphere, L1/softmax -> simplex
x̂ = W_d h̃ + b_d
```

This throws away the absolute activation magnitude and keeps only the
*distributional* information: **which features fire and in what proportion**.
An embedding becomes a *composition of concepts* — a topic-model-like reading
(L1/softmax give a literal distribution over concepts). With unit-norm inputs
and unit-norm decoder columns, normalising `h` also pushes `‖x̂‖ ≈ 1`, so the
reconstruction stays on the sphere "for free", and the reconstruction objective
aligns with the cosine metric that retrieval actually uses.

Latent-normalisation modes (`spherical_sae/model.py:normalize_latent`):

| mode      | manifold        | reading                                  |
|-----------|-----------------|------------------------------------------|
| `none`    | —               | standard SAE (baseline)                  |
| `l2`      | sphere `S^{k-1}`| directional / compositional              |
| `l1`      | simplex         | true probability distribution over concepts |
| `softmax` | simplex (smooth)| smooth distribution over active concepts |

## Layout

```
spherical_sae/
├── papers/2408.00657v2.pdf        # the reference paper
├── spherical_sae/
│   ├── model.py                   # SphericalSAE: top-k encoder + normalize_latent + decoder
│   ├── data.py                    # synthetic spherical generator + .npy loader
│   └── train.py                   # training loop + metrics (mse / cosine / nmse)
├── scripts/
│   └── build_dataset.py           # download + align the ArXiv-ML dataset
└── data/                          # (gitignored) downloaded + built dataset
```

## Setup

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
pip install --upgrade pip
pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
pip install numpy huggingface_hub datasets pyarrow pandas
```

## Dataset

We combine two HuggingFace datasets by **CShorten** (aligned by row order):

- [`CShorten/ML-ArXiv-Papers`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/CShorten/ML-ArXiv-Papers)
  — `title`, `abstract` (117,592 ML arXiv papers).
- [`CShorten/ArXiv-ML-Abstract-Embeddings`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/CShorten/ArXiv-ML-Abstract-Embeddings)
  — **384-dim** abstract embeddings (raw, not unit-norm; consistent with
  `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`), one per paper. The loader L2-normalises them onto the sphere.

Build it (downloads ~670 MB into the gitignored `data/`):

```bash
python scripts/build_dataset.py
```

This verifies the two sources have matching row counts and writes:

- `data/embeddings.npy` — `float32 [N, 384]`, ready for the SAE loader
- `data/papers.parquet` — `title`, `abstract`
- `data/meta.json` — shapes + provenance

## Train

Smoke test on synthetic spherical data (compares all latent-norm modes):

```bash
python -m spherical_sae.train
```

On the real embeddings:

```bash
python -m spherical_sae.train --embeddings data/embeddings.npy --latent-norm l2
```

Embeddings are L2-normalised onto the sphere by the loader. The cosine
similarity of the reconstruction is the metric to watch — the spherical
variant aims to match the standard SAE there while discarding magnitude.

### Dead-latent revival (AuxK)

Top-k SAEs tend to leave some latents permanently silent ("dead"). Following
Gao et al. (2024) — the *ghost-grads* / AuxK trick from the paper — we add an
auxiliary loss: among the latents that have not fired for ~one epoch, take the
top `k_aux` (default `2k`) and use them to reconstruct the **residual**
`e = x − x̂`. This gives the dead latents gradient and revives them:

```
L = L_recon(x, x̂) + α · ‖ e − W_d z_aux ‖²      # z_aux = top-k_aux dead latents
```

The residual is detached, so the auxiliary path only trains the dead latents
(and their decoder columns) without perturbing the main reconstruction. The
dead variant `l2` benefits most, since latent normalisation otherwise leaves
more latents silent. Implemented in `model.py` (`aux_decode`, `update_dead_stats`).

### Full-dataset training

```bash
python scripts/train_full.py --modes none l2 \
    --n-latents 4096 --k 32 --k-aux 64 --steps 8000 --batch-size 2048
```

Trains one SAE per latent-norm mode on all 117,592 embeddings (linear lr decay,
batched full-dataset evaluation), then writes:

- `data/checkpoints/sae_<mode>_<tag>.pt` — weights + config (gitignored)
- `results/metrics_<tag>.json` — cos_sim, nmse, dead-latent count, mean active (versioned)
